expectations.name: default-review-of-a-flawed-srd
expected_behavior: Reads the whole SRD, then writes `specs/login.review.md` — and makes no edit to `login.md`
Groups findings by document section
Tags the two-rule requirement `[blocker, atomicity]` citing REQ-1, and the uncovered scope item `[blocker, coverage]` citing SCO-2
Collects the British spelling into the `## Errata` block at the top, tagged `[minor, linguistic]` citing `(SRD:house)`, stated as the substitution `` `behaviour` → `behavior` ``
Closes with a per-severity count and whether a blocker stands between the SRD and the Quality Bar
The closing per-severity counts match what the review file actually contains — a tally is a claim about the file, and a wrong one sends the author to the wrong findings

expectations.name: applies-rules-create-only-stubs
expected_behavior: Flags the single owner (STR-2), the missing Initiative link (STR-3), and `ACCEPTED` without an approved design (STA-2), all as blockers, none excused as an authoring placeholder
Raises no back-link finding: STR-4/6 live in external systems
Records all three under the Metadata section of the review file

expectations.name: check-a-prior-review
expected_behavior: Classifies each open finding fixed / partial / not-addressed / invalid (or labels that map one-to-one onto those) against the current text, in a short status table keyed by finding number
Re-verifies only — hunts for no new defects
Ticks fixed findings and moves them to `## Resolved`, keeping their numbers
Annotates partials with `*(Partial — …)*` and moves the invalid finding to `## Withdrawn` with a reason
Bumps the `updated:` frontmatter timestamp and reuses no number

expectations.name: feedback-export-for-a-ticket
expected_behavior: Emits plain text grouped by section heading, one bullet per open issue, and writes no file
Lists the `Errata` group first, since it holds open findings
Keeps each finding's number and the SRD's own requirement id in the form `#<n> <requirement id>:` but drops the checkbox, rule-id citations, and severity tags
Uses no markdown beyond bullets — it is going into a ticket or an email
Lists open findings only, omitting Resolved and Withdrawn

expectations.name: walk-records-only-confirmed-findings
expected_behavior: Goes section by section, presenting each section's findings and waiting for the user's answer: the review file gains a section's findings only in a turn after the user confirmed them
Writes only the confirmed findings to `login.review.md`, as author-facing guidance
Never edits `login.md`

expectations.name: fixture-regression
expected_behavior: Finds GR-1 non-atomic (REQ-1) and the duplicate id GR-3 (REQ-3)
Finds "fast" unverifiable (REQ-6)
Finds SC-2 uncovered (SCO-2) and GR-4 contradicting OSC-1 (SCO-3)
Finds behaviour stated inside the Export Job glossary entry (GLO-1/2)
Finds the single owner (STR-2) and the missing Initiative link (STR-3)
Finds `ACCEPTED` with an unapproved design and an unmet Quality Bar (STA-2 / STA-3)
Finds MUST used in the Introduction (LANG-3)
Collects the British spellings `colourise` and `dialogue` as minor findings under `## Errata`
Finds the keyword notice citing RFC 8174 alone, with the RFC 2119 reference missing (STR-8), and collects it under `## Errata` as one substitution replacing the whole notice
Finds the `Designs` placeholder left in an `ACCEPTED` SRD whose GR-3 changes the UI (STR-5)
Finds the second GR-3 describing how the badge looks rather than what the system does (LANG-5)
Finds GR-4's "export run" drifting from the glossary's Export Job

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the result — no preamble, no narration of reading the SRD
Writes the findings to the review file and closes with a short pointer plus per-severity counts
Does not re-list in chat the findings it just wrote to the file

expectations.name: errata-re-sort
expected_behavior: Moves `#4` into a `## Errata` block at the top, keeping its number, `[minor]` tag, category, and citation
Rewrites its prose fix into the substitution shape that makes it appliable unreviewed
Leaves the blocker `#2` under its own section
Reclassifies only — hunts no new defects
Bumps `updated:` because something moved, and reports the moved number
Reads the SRD to quote the `old` text exactly when rewriting the prose fix, while editing only the review file
Run twice in a row, the second run changes nothing at all — not a moved finding, not a fresh `updated:` timestamp

expectations.name: facts-vs-corpus-routes-doc-gaps
expected_behavior: Runs the draft check first and, on the prior session's drafts, invokes `srd:report-doc-gap` to drain them before any corpus search

Routes the unconfirmable `GW-2` retry count to `srd:report-doc-gap` as a draft gap and files no finding against it in `gateway.review.md` — an unconfirmable claim becomes a draft gap, never a review finding. Quoting the claim inside some other finding is not the test; where the gap went is
Records the contradicted `GW-5` timeout as a `reference` finding in the review file
After the closing tally, offers to work the `GW-2` draft gap now or later, and never files it silently

expectations.name: no-drafts-skip-the-delegate
expected_behavior: Echoes the draft-check result and invokes `srd:report-doc-gap` neither at the start nor at the close — no draft exists, and this run captured nothing to offer
Raises no `reference` finding and captures no gap: the SRD asserts no platform fact
Creates `specs/login.review.md` and writes the three defects with fresh numbers from `#1`
The reply leads with the outcome — findings and the tally — with no narrated startup sequence ("first I check…, then I read…"); the one-clause draft-check result bullet 1 asks for is not narration

expectations.name: gate-stops-without-project-config
expected_behavior: Stops in one line naming the failed check: `project-config.md` not found in the start directory or any parent
Reads no part of the SRD, calls no server tool, and runs no draft check before stopping
Writes no `specs/login.review.md` and asks the user nothing
